title: Only the decision owner approves a team's decision, and an approved decision is never edited
request: Package T5a of the team workspace plan (Part A, item 1): today one person can record another person's approval of a team's decision. Enforce who approves, add a revision and a request identity, record every write and refusal, and make DCLAB_AUTH=none mean no sign-in everywhere.
spec: dclab-core 0.169.0: TeamDecision v2 (revision, request_id, supersedes, outcome_at, outcome_by, outcome_measure, policy_ref; reads v1 at revision 1), TeamWork v2, the pure rule decision_write(stored, new, actor, may_approve_role) returning a DecisionVerdict. ExperienceEvent v19 with team.decision.recorded/approved/refused and team.correction.applied/refused; ledger points team.decision_approve and team.correction_accept. dclab_rnd: teamspace/store.py record_decision(home, scope, decision, *, actor, expected_revision, request_id) judged under the problem base's lock through memory/bases.py link_dependents(guard=); DecisionRefused; ledger/capture.py team_decision_approved and team_correction_accepted (the second for package T2); memory/scope.py auth_enabled reads the normalised setting (accounts/principal.py auth_mode). Files and PostgreSQL, no migration.
plan: read how a decision is stored today (the problem base's ledger) and where roles are checked
failing tests first: the rule's cases in the core, then the store's (another person's approval, an agent, a stale click, two approvals at once, a retry, an edit after approval, DCLAB_AUTH=none)
TeamDecision v2 reading v1, and decision_write, in dclab_core
the event kinds, the ledger points and the two capture writers, for T5a and T2 in one experience version
record_decision judged inside the base's locked change, with its events and the approval's ledger record
independent review, its fixes with tests, the tests on files and PostgreSQL, the wheel check

decisions.decision: Judge the write inside the problem base's change (a guard passed to link_dependents), not before it
decisions.why: the rule must read the same stored record the write replaces; a check before the lock lets two approvals at once both pass. One guard gives files (folder lock) and PostgreSQL (advisory lock, version check, rollback) the same behaviour with no migration

decisions.decision: A change to an approved decision is a new decision naming supersedes, never an edit
decisions.why: whoever acted on the first approval must still be able to read exactly what was approved; the owner's test is approve 50, correct to 30, re-approve

decisions.decision: TeamWork moves to v2 with TeamDecision
decisions.why: the contracts' rule: a change in a contained model moves the container's version, since readers refuse unknown fields; v1 documents read unchanged

decisions.decision: A person named as the actor must be the scope's own principal; an agent may record a proposal or a follow-up but the rule refuses it every approval
decisions.why: the scope is what the server verified; an actor argument that could name anyone would move the old hole (sara writing dana's approval) from the document to the argument

decisions.decision: A repeated request id returns the stored entry only when the actor and content are the same (moments aside); the same id on another write is refused
decisions.why: the reviewer showed a reused id answered an approval attempt with the unapproved entry as if it had been kept; excluding the moments keeps a retry stamped a second later a retry

decisions.decision: auth_enabled follows the server's normalised setting exactly (password or oidc, else none)
decisions.why: the server and the worker refuse to start on a mistyped DCLAB_AUTH, so the two readings can no longer disagree; before, 'none' made the scope refuse the local owner the server had let in

decisions.decision: The approval's ledger record is a person's answer only, with counts and one flag as its state
decisions.why: no rule and no agent approves, and a state never holds the option's words or a table's value

change: dclab_core/team_work.py (TeamDecision v2, DecisionVerdict, decision_write, TeamWork v2), experience.py (v19, five kinds), ledger.py (two points, five state fields), workflow_labels.py, adapters/conformance.py, adapters/main_product_experience.py, schemas and three baselines, CHANGELOG, 0.169.0; dclab_rnd/teamspace/store.py (record_decision, DecisionRefused), memory/bases.py (link_dependents guard, requests), memory/scope.py, accounts/principal.py, settings.py, ledger/capture.py, ledger/__init__.py; docs/guides/CORE_INTEGRATION.md; tests.

findings.defect: one person could record another person's approval of a team's decision
findings.scenario: sara (ML engineer) calls record_decision with a decision whose approval names dana: the approval is stored and read back as dana's
findings.cause: record_decision checked only that the caller may write, the problem and the citations; the contract checked only that the approval names the owner; approve_decision was enforced nowhere
findings.fix: decision_write under the base's lock: the actor is the decision owner in person and holds approve_decision; a person actor must be the scope's principal; an agent or team actor is refused

findings.defect: a later record replaced the stored decision whole, with no revision and no request identity
findings.scenario: dana approves while sara changes the option; or a click is sent twice after a lost answer: the last write wins silently, or a second approval is stored
findings.cause: the ledger kept the last document given for a ref
findings.fix: each kept write is the next revision; expected_revision refuses a stale one as a RevisionConflictError; a repeated request id returns the stored entry; an approved decision's option, citations, policy and approval are immutable

findings.defect: with DCLAB_AUTH=none the local owner was refused its own team threads
findings.scenario: DCLAB_AUTH=none, open a team thread as the local owner: 403 Not yours to read
findings.cause: auth_enabled was bool(DCLAB_AUTH), so 'none' counted as sign-in on, while the server's settings read it as off; access() then asked for a user id the local owner does not have
findings.fix: accounts/principal.py auth_mode is the one reading; the settings validator and auth_enabled both use it
findings.test: tests/test_teamspace_threads.py AuthNoneRoutesTests (the local owner's route tests again under DCLAB_AUTH=none, and test_none_is_read_as_no_sign_in_by_the_scope_and_the_settings_alike); run against the old reading it fails with the 403

findings.defect: link_dependents called with a decision's document and no guard stored an approval unjudged
findings.scenario: bases.link_dependents(home, sara_scope, [{ref: team_decision:D-6, kind: team_decision, doc: D-6 with dana's approval}]): stored, with no event, no ledger record and no revision
findings.cause: the guard was optional and the old path that keeps any document stayed open beside it
findings.fix: a link carrying a doc without a guard is refused before the base is touched

findings.defect: another person could take over an approved decision through supersedes
findings.scenario: dana approves D-1; mia (owner role) records D-2 with decision_owner mia, supersedes D-1 and her own approval: kept
findings.cause: only the existence of the superseded decision was checked; the pure rule sees one decision
findings.fix: the host refuses (owner_changed) a decision that supersedes another owner's decision

findings.defect: a sentence could reach an event as a meta field
findings.scenario: approve with policy_ref 'Refund policy: customers of ACME get 40% off until March': the whole sentence in team.decision.approved.policy
findings.cause: policy_ref and outcome_measure were free text up to 300 characters
findings.fix: both carry the id pattern in the contract (v2 was not released): a reference and a name

findings.defect: a reused request id swallowed a different write silently
findings.scenario: propose with request r1, then an approval sent with r1: the unapproved entry comes back as if kept, and no refusal is recorded
findings.cause: the repeat check compared the id alone, before any other check
findings.fix: each remembered id keeps a fingerprint of the actor and content; the same id on another write is refused as request_reused and recorded

findings.defect: a recorded outcome could be rewritten or erased in place by any writer, an agent too
findings.scenario: after approval an agent writes an outcome, then another, then removes it: all three kept; leaving outcome_by empty avoided the check of who records
findings.cause: the rule froze what the approval covers but not the outcome, and checked outcome_by only when it was given
findings.fix: a kept outcome is immutable; an outcome names the actor as its recorder

findings.defect: tests/test_memory_bases_storage.py test_racing_processes_on_one_revision_leave_one_winner failed once in four runs on PostgreSQL
findings.scenario: two processes open the same new workspace at once: the second insert of its workspace row fails with a duplicate primary key (pk_workspace), before any base is written
findings.cause: the insert says on conflict (key) do nothing, but two racing inserts collide on the id; storage/db.py, not touched by this package
findings.fix: not fixed here: outside this package's files; rerun three times, three passes; reported to the main session
findings.open: storage/db.py workspace_for: the insert should ignore a conflict on the id too

outcome: An approval is kept only for the decision owner in person holding approve_decision; every write has a revision, stale and repeated writes are handled, an approved decision and a recorded outcome are never edited, every write and refusal is recorded, and DCLAB_AUTH=none is no sign-in everywhere. The routes and the approval control are T5b.
lessons: Adding a guarded path is not enough: close the unguarded one beside it, or the hole only moves.
A pure rule that sees one record cannot protect a link between two records; say in its contract what the host owes.
A free-text field that an event copies is a privacy field: give references and names an id's pattern.
An idempotency key needs a fingerprint of what it wrote, or it answers a different write with success.
risks: approval.when is the caller's; T5b's route should stamp it on the server.
A decision whose owner left cannot be superseded by another person: that needs an owner's hand-over rule, not built here.
The data catalog is stale until make catalog; no route or page uses record_decision yet (T5b).
The ledger point team.correction_accept and the two correction kinds are declared here and written by T2.
